# Original Windows bit-reset consumer

This self-authored header-free C function calls the Windows `_interlockedbittestandreset` intrinsic with bit index 5 and returns its previous value as a `u32`. The declaration matches the installed clang `intrin.h`: `unsigned char _interlockedbittestandreset(long volatile *, long)`. The Windows i686 target makes `long` 32 bits, checked by a source assertion. The source uses the intrinsic declaration and pragma; it contains no inline assembly.

The [Microsoft intrinsic contract](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cpp/intrinsics/interlockedbittestandreset-intrinsic-functions?view=msvc-170) describes clearing the bit and returning its previous value through the x86 LOCK BTR implementation. Its displayed syntax omits the volatile qualifier; the installed compiler declaration and Microsoft's common intrinsic table include it. The source retains the compiler-compatible declaration explicitly.

The builder imports the unchanged scalar i686 profile and strict ordinary COFF extractor from `../p2-compiled-records/build.py`, SHA256 `fe426f202b48664a87357c766d39099b9d35b5d8217c2b114696164a0d468258`. Only the extractor's function symbol and diagnostic spelling change from `ring3_reduce` to `ring3_reset_bit`. Flags, environment, tools and COFF constraints remain fixed. A fresh output directory, tool versions, argv, source/builder/tool hashes and post-build input stability are recorded. Routine tests consume retained artifacts without invoking a compiler.

Two root-run discovery builds produced the identical whole original 19-byte text `8b4c2404ba0500000031c0f00fb3110f92c0c3`, SHA256 `763a610207cf2d28842dcc398e727cb96611775b4ccb539e706d361d7ca391d1`. The original COFF is 536 bytes, SHA256 `a89cace6204c9ba0d0ac345a765854340bb75f557a11deea48774d4a8b635bb6`. The original C is 341 bytes, SHA256 `55e500954268e21be8a42322e927fca139534964d5c5abbf85646b465444e960`; the Intel disassembly is 475 bytes, SHA256 `aa88aa37bcb0e21147babf8930d68cf3f711c1e118ec6ed36df88f457ac97080`. The only code section is `.text`; `.data` and `.bss` are empty, and `.debug$S` has 100 bytes of compiler metadata. There are no relocations or unresolved external symbols. A formal fixture build is required to reproduce the discovery C, object, text and disassembly before artifact publication.

The complete six-instruction original function loads its pointer, sets EDX to 5, clears EAX, executes register-index LOCK BTR at offset 11, sets AL from CF and naturally returns. The original XOR makes both raw `u32` returns exactly 0 or 1. A separately authored guest caller will call this unchanged original twice on one live cell, pause before the first LOCK, and consume `first | (second << 1)` into 1. The cell starts at `0xa5a55a7a`; the first call clears bit 5 to produce `0xa5a55a5a` and returns 1. The second call performs an already-clear identity write and returns 0. CPU and RAM remain live between calls. The caller is distinct from the compiler-produced function.

The product scope is exact `F0 0F B3 /r` memory DWORD with a register bit index. The CPU selects the signed bit-string DWORD and normalized bit; one checked canonical helper returns the old full DWORD after complete Read4 and mandatory Write4 preflight. Already-clear identity is still a write. Ring3's existing deterministic undefined-flag policy is `(incoming & 0x442) | oldbit`; it retains ZF/DF/fixed bit 1 and clears the other undefined arithmetic flags. This policy is separate from Intel's defined CF and unchanged ZF requirements.

Actual evidence is planned in all four bound profiles with a valid dirty 4364-byte arena, canonical helper receipts, selected RAM/canaries, precise faults and repair, currentness, malformed nonforwarding packets and consumed-code identity writes. Observed counts and review results belong to the evidence bank and `result.json`; this provenance is stable before execution. The proof is finite private flat32 synchronous unshared execution. It makes no hardware locking, Windows concurrency, shared-memory ordering, full-RAM, compatibility or performance claim. The [R3-552 task](https://linear.app/ring3-dev/issue/R3-552) records the selected contract.
